title: Correct refractive index
description: Essential Criteria: The final answer for part (1) must be n = tan θ.

title: Correct ray separation
description: Essential Criteria: The final answer for part (2) must be d = D tan θ.

title: Angle relationship application
description: Important Criteria: The solution must correctly apply the condition that the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular, establishing γ = 90° - θ.

title: Snell's Law application
description: Important Criteria: The solution must correctly apply Snell's law, n = sin θ / sin γ, to relate the angles and refractive index.

title: Trigonometric simplification
description: Important Criteria: The solution must correctly simplify the expression using the identity sin(90° - θ) = cos θ to obtain tan θ.

title: Geometry for ray separation
description: Important Criteria: The solution must correctly use geometry (e.g., parallel lines and trigonometry) to relate the incident separation D to the refracted separation d.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional Criteria: The solution may note that both n and d/tan θ are dimensionless, confirming the distance d has the same unit as D.

title: Misapplied angle condition
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student incorrectly interprets the perpendicular ray condition, e.g., setting θ = γ or θ + γ = 90° for the wrong rays.

title: Sign or direction error
description: Pitfall Criteria: Penalize if the student incorrectly uses the law of reflection (i = r) to alter the angle for Snell's law, or misidentifies the incident medium.
